Observed ranks 0–6 for q=2: (4,4,72,112,704,1408,1792); for q=3: (9,18,648,2646,25110,122472,380538). The resulting probabilities are 77/2048 and 169/59049.
correctness.rationale: The commutator has zero diagonal and the three upper coordinates give the stated 3×5 map over R after removing a free scalar diagonal. The residue rank-two cases follow by testing when the third row is in the span of the first two: if both are nonzero this requires a≠0, b=−a and aw+uv=0, while a zero first or second row gives the other two cases. Their closures are the two coordinate 3-flats and V(a+b,aw+uv); the last is an irreducible dimension-three hypersurface in the four-space a+b=0 (primitive linear in w with coprime coefficients). Unit elimination leaves εK and gives field rank 2r+rank(K), with K the map induced by the first-order part from the residue kernel to the cokernel. At the rank-one residue w≠0 the kernel condition is t=−s, and K is the stated two-row matrix; rank one counts 2(q²−1) possibilities with exactly one nonzero row plus (q−1)² with both supported in the third column. At rank two with a=u=0 and b≠0, y12 and s are independently free in the residue kernel and K=0 requires a1=u1=0. When a=b=u=0 and v≠0 the relation y12=−ws/v leaves only one linear condition. Reversing indices and transposing gives the other zero-row stratum. In the nonzero-a stratum the residual row after pivoting on a,b is (a+b,−(aw+uv)/a,(−bw+uv)/b); its differentials impose exactly two independent conditions since the last two numerators differ by (a+b)w and a≠0. All these statements hold in characteristic two. Thus the two rank-two types give 3q²(q−1) and 2q(q−1) residue points, with q³ and q⁴ rank-four lifts per point respectively. Adding all lifts and restoring the scalar factor q² yields the seven coefficients in the Finding, positive for q≥2 and summing to q^12. Weighting by q^(12−r) gives the stated commuting probability.
residual_risks: The direct multiplication check exhausts only the two prime fields, not all extension fields or lengths; the all-q conclusion and geometric components follow from the proof. The component statement is set-theoretic and does not assert any scheme multiplicity.

value.rationale: The whole adjoint-rank distribution is a natural exact refinement of the commuting probability: it records how often a typical first argument has each possible number of commuting partners. The simplest nonfield length already has two lift patterns at the same residue rank, explained by the component intersections rather than by interpolation of prime-field counts. The classification and geometric cause of the exceptional lift counts are useful in their own right, independently of the previously covered probability consequence.
residual_risks: No length-three-or-higher rank classification or application to nonsplit rings is inferred.
